# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration 7. Parent = cand_0003 (current champion, val 0.637). Scoring: the agent's FINAL
code is text-substituted (`1_<id>_input`→`2_`/`3_`) and re-run on two hidden inputs of the
same layout; a task counts only if ALL 3 match answer_position. Signatures: `[1,0,*]` =
passes preview, fails hidden re-run (generalization/edge gap); `[0,0,0]` = wrong on the
preview too (comprehension error, grader/type fault, or environment fault).

## HEADLINE OUTCOME: documented CEILING — no speculative edit shipped
After a full re-diagnosis of THIS iteration's 33 failing traces I found **no edit that
passes all three tests (REAL, SAFE, VERIFIED) and has not already been refuted** by a prior
RESULT. The clean prose surface was harvested by cand_0001–0003; the last three iterations
(0004/0005/0006) each shipped one more edit and were **all rejected with large negative Δ**
(−0.077, −0.077, −0.088), fixing 0 stable tasks between them. This iteration's job was to
verify whether any winnable cluster remains and, finding none, to hand back the ceiling with
hard evidence rather than ship a fourth speculative edit that would (a) fail the VERIFIED
test and (b) only re-perturb the flaky boundary tasks. Per the framework's guidance, an
accurate "here is the ceiling, here is the evidence" handback is the correct action. The
capability files are therefore **unchanged** (identical to champion cand_0003); the gate
will reject a net-zero candidate and correctly preserve the champion.

## WHY the gate cannot be beaten by a safe prose edit here (the noise-dominated plateau)
The broke sets of the three rejected iterations overlap heavily on the SAME tasks:
- cand_0004 broke {18137, 253-22, 347-49, 47699, 50486, 53957, 56561}
- cand_0005 broke {31420, 36478, 47699, 49237, 50486, 50682, 56561}
- cand_0006 broke {253-22, 2768, 31420, 347-49, 36478, 45581, 49237, 50486, 53957, 56561}
Tasks **50486, 56561, 47699, 36478, 31420, 253-22, 347-49, 49237, 53957** recur in almost
every broke set — and several of them ALSO appear in the FIXED sets of cand_0001–0003. A
task that is broken by one edit and fixed by another, across unrelated edits, is not being
controlled by the prompt: it is a **flaky near-boundary task** flipping on the reader's
stochastic code generation (seed=0 but azure/gpt-5.5 is not deterministic). The run-to-run
noise is ≈ ±6–10 tasks. Any safe additive edit's *deterministic* gain must clear that noise
band to be accepted. There is no remaining stable-failing cluster large enough to do so.

## Ranked diagnosis of the 33 failing tasks (THIS iteration's ./trajectories/)
| bucket | tasks | why unwinnable by a SAFE prose edit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **GRADER / type-strictness fault (agent output provably CORRECT)** — NEW evidence | 50755, 55258, 585-41, 4225 | The agent's saved cells match the instruction's own stated/expected values, yet score 0. Editing the prompt cannot fix a grader that rejects a correct value. |
| **Flaky near-boundary generalization (noise)** | 30930, 32975, 42930, 48983, 49782, 53305, 58484, 58890, 250-20 | `[1,0,*]` — operation is right, flips on hidden re-run/stochasticity. Boundary/composite-key/run-segment prose already present (cand_0002/0003). cand_0004's executed self-test targeting exactly these was REJECTED (−0.077). |
| **Comprehension / underspecified, NO gold in trace** | 269-44, 398-14, 413-15, 157-4, 146-49, 577-40, 254-34, 32468, 39946, 53449, 55039, 50526, 10281, 6698 | Emitted code already generalizes; it implements a different-but-defensible reading of an ambiguous spec. No ground truth in the traces → no interpretation is VERIFIABLE → every fix fails the VERIFIED/SAFE tests and risks leaking a task-specific reading. |
| **Volatile "current date"** | 34-5, 32023 | "current month"/TODAY() resolved at benchmark-creation time, not grade time (today=2026-08-02). Unknowable reference date. |
| **Recalc / unreadable-file environment fault** | 45944, 14207, 53062, 55912 | Formula recalculation / invalid xlsx — infra, explicitly "not a prompt defect" in prior feedback. |

## VERIFY-THE-FIX evidence for the two edits I DESIGNED and then DROPPED (disproven)
- **Dropped "positional Nth-value" worked example** (target 50755): read the agent's final
  code — `nums_sorted = sorted(nums, reverse=True); result = nums_sorted[1] - nums_sorted[2]`.
  I hand-checked all 5 columns against the visible "Expected result" row: B 57−32=25, C
  82−79=3, D 146−121=25 (ranked, since sheet order is 162,146,117,121), E 202−180=22, F
  286−226=60 → the agent output is **exactly [25,3,25,22,60] = the expected values**. So
  50755 genuinely means "2nd/3rd LARGEST" (ranked), the agent already does that correctly,
  and it STILL scores 0 → grader/type fault (agent downcasts 25.0→int 25; expected shows
  25.0). A positional edit would have made a CORRECT task wrong. DROPPED as disproven +
  unsafe (it also contradicts prompt line 22, which helps other tasks).
- **Dropped "preserve commas ⇒ write text" contract** (target 585-41): read the agent's
  verification print — it ALREADY writes `'11,604.67'` (str, comma preserved) etc., exactly
  the instruction's ask, and still fails instances 1&2 (`[0,0,1]`). The comma-string reading
  is already what the agent does; the failure is grader/type strictness, not a missing rule.
  DROPPED as disproven.
- **Not re-shipped: macro/VBA-source-in-cell** (cand_0006): verified real for 254-34 (agent
  dumps a `Sub…End Sub` string into C2) and safe, but cand_0006 was the WHOLE batch of exactly
  this edit and was REJECTED, and its RESULT shows it did NOT even flip 254-34 (254-34 ∉
  fixed) — 254-34 is underspecified (a single cell C2 for a subset-sum *highlighting* task;
  the agent cannot know what scalar to write). Re-submitting a rejected whole-batch is
  explicitly forbidden and would not fix its target.

## Confirmed-SAFE checks
- Placeholders: all six required + {max_turns} present in task_template.md; prompt.md has
  zero `{`/`}`. Capability files unchanged this iteration → zero regression risk by
  construction.

## Process & features used
- Compact dump of all 33 failing traces (instruction, answer_position, preview, feedback,
  final emitted code) via a read-only python script; deep-read the final code + verification
  output for 50755, 55258, 585-41, 4225, 6698, 254-34, 398-14, 413-15, 577-40, 157-4, 146-49,
  269-44. Cross-read LEDGER (broke/fixed overlap), JOURNAL (refuted hypotheses), and cand_0003
  PROCESS. No subagents needed at this scale.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do NOT touch)
- cand_0001 RE-RUN/generalization block, cand_0002 composite-key/blank-vs-zero/example blocks,
  cand_0003 boundary-segment + run-to-completion bullets, and the verify-before-finish round —
  these are the load-bearing fixes that took the champion from 0.538→0.637.
- Do NOT ban Excel formulas globally (35747/37962/45581/49237/54675 pass via formulas —
  re-verified as a standing refutation).
- Do NOT re-tighten verify item (a) to "every cell holds a value" (399-14 regression).

## Deliberately skipped + PLATEAU / lever recommendation
- Skipped every comprehension `[0,0,0]` (no gold → unverifiable) and every environment/grader
  fault (not mine to work around).
- PLATEAU is confirmed: +0.066 (cand_0003) → three consecutive rejections. The prompt lever is
  exhausted. The residual is NOT a knowledge gap the prose can close — it is (1) a grader that
  rejects provably-correct outputs (50755/55258/585-41/4225), (2) unknowable-gold comprehension
  tasks, and (3) reader stochasticity on boundary tasks. None of these move on prompt wording.
  The honest next lever is OUTSIDE the prompt: fix the grader's type/format strictness, pin the
  volatile reference date, or lower reader temperature — all of which are infrastructure the
  optimizer may not edit. I hand this back rather than ship a fourth speculative edit.
